T-002.Title: Register preserves enabled unless the incoming request grows; growth resets into the #298 re-approval path and the epoch keeps bumping

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/registry.rs register consults the entry already stored under the same id and preserves its enabled flag whenever the incoming manifest requests no incoming capability that the stored manifest did not already request: the comparison runs over the incoming capability vocabulary only — a capability name counts when it is in super::live_server::incoming_capability_names(), the same pub(in m045_ext) set the #298 enable coverage gate consults (live_server.rs:897) — so shrinking or equal incoming sets preserve the flag and non-incoming capability changes never affect the decision. The decision is computed inside the existing extensions Mutex lock discipline with no new lock; the stored manifest and the fresh health always update; a first registration for a fresh id keeps enabled: false exactly as today; the doc comment "Overwrites any previous entry" is rewritten to the preservation truth.

Growth is honest: when the re-discovered manifest requests an incoming name the previously stored manifest did not, register resets enabled to false with the distinct BLOCK_REGISTER_GROWTH_RESET log carrying the id, so the owner's next enable passes through the #298 coverage gate (mod.rs:140-174) and refuses into ext_enable_reapproval_required when the stored pairing grant does not cover the grown set — the gallery already surfaces that instruction (index.vue:207-212). This restores the coverage gate's invariant: an enabled extension's manifest was covered by its stored grant at the last enable.

Every registration keeps bumping the authorization_epoch: the fetch_add at registry.rs:101 stays unconditional, so an in-flight credential that crosses a re-discovery is fenced exactly as today and register's participation in the invalidation semantics of C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH/#298 is unchanged; the T-001 pin registry_re_register_still_bumps_authorization_epoch turns from insurance into the enforced contract.

T-003.Title: Honest no-op toggles: duplicate enable and verified-absent disable return Ok without fencing, without revocation, without an epoch bump

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/mod.rs mt_ext_enable: the #326 revoke-pending marker gate (121-131) keeps running first exactly as today; AFTER it, when the registry already reports the extension enabled (the enabled-only Ok of registry.authorization_epoch doubles as the query), the command logs the distinct BLOCK_ENABLE_ALREADY_ENABLED and returns Ok — without minting, without the coverage gate, without taking stream_gate and without an epoch bump; every other id flows through the unchanged mint (134-138), coverage gate (140-174) and stream_gate + enable (176-179) path.

src-tauri/src/m045_ext/mod.rs mt_ext_disable takes its no-op decision BEFORE the fence block (191) from three reads that hold neither gate nor session lock (the native credential I/O precedent), in order: the marker read auth::get_revoke_pending — this read IS executed on every disable and is never skipped or short-circuited by a registry-only pre-check; the keyring I/O deliberately precedes any gate so a standing or unreadable marker is always seen before the decision; the strict secret read auth::verify_secret_absent (an unreadable persistent store can never mean absent); and the registry state read (registered-and-disabled = peek_manifest Some AND authorization_epoch Err). Only when all three agree — marker Ok(false), secret verifiably absent, id registered and disabled — the command logs the distinct BLOCK_DISABLE_ALREADY_ABSENT and returns Ok: no gate, no revocation retry, no marker record or clear, no grant revoke, no context drain replay, no epoch bump. Any other combination — any marker error, a standing marker, a surviving or unreadable secret, an enabled or unregistered id — sends the full existing path (fence, disable, drain, revoke, marker record/clear, grant revoke) exactly as today (191-273).

The #326 recovery is intact: a standing marker always sends the full revocation retry (the ext_disable_revoke_failed fail_delete pattern and the clear-on-proof semantics unchanged), the BLOCK_DISABLE_REVOKE_PENDING_UNRECORDED residual (a surviving secret with no marker) always re-enters the full path through the verify_secret_absent leg, the strict-absence success condition and every existing BLOCK_ log name are unchanged, and the double-disable success leg of disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence (tests.rs:1824-1825) now passes by explicit no-op instead of harness luck — a duplicate toggle no longer fences in-flight credentials because the no-op paths bump no epoch.
